n: As the Church grows, a complaint arises: Greek-speaking Jewish believers feel their widows are overlooked in the daily distribution of food compared with those of Aramaic-speaking believers. Growth brings new problems.

f.g: Hellenists — Jews raised outside the land of Israel whose main language was Greek.
Jews of the homeland who spoke Aramaic (and Hebrew).

n: The Twelve call the whole body of disciples together and explain that it wouldn’t be right for them to neglect preaching God’s word to manage food distribution.

f.g: It is not right or fitting.
Handle the daily food distribution (and perhaps its finances).

n: They ask the members to select seven men with good reputations, full of the Spirit and wisdom, to oversee this work. Even practical service requires spiritual qualifications.

f.w: full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom

n: The apostles will devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word — wise delegation lets each do what they are called to do.
The idea pleases everyone. They choose seven men, all with Greek names — likely from the very group that felt neglected. Stephen and Philip will become key figures in the chapters ahead.

f.w: Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost

f.g: Not the apostle Philip but “Philip the evangelist.”
A Gentile convert to Judaism from Antioch in Syria.

n: The congregation presents them to the apostles, who pray and lay their hands on them — setting them apart with authority for their calling.

f.w: they laid their hands on them
f.r: Numbers 27:18-23; Acts 13:3; Articles of Faith 1:5; D&C 42:11

n: God’s word keeps spreading, the number of disciples in Jerusalem grows rapidly, and even many priests accept the faith.

f.w: a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith
f.g: Probably ordinary priests serving in rotation at the temple, not the elite high-priestly families.

n: Stephen, full of grace and power, performs great wonders and signs among the people. His calling to serve tables didn’t limit his spiritual influence.
Opposition rises from members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen — Jews from North Africa and Asia Minor — who debate with Stephen. Saul of Tarsus, from Cilicia, may well have been among them.

f.g: Libertines = Freedmen — descendants of Jews once enslaved and later freed, perhaps by Rome.
A region in southeastern Asia Minor whose chief city was Tarsus, Paul’s hometown.

n: They can’t stand against the wisdom and Spirit with which he speaks — just as Jesus had promised.

f.w: they were not able to resist the wisdom

n: So they secretly put men up to claiming they heard Stephen speak blasphemy against Moses and God — the same tactic used against Jesus.

f.g: suborned = secretly bribed or induced to give false testimony.

n: They stir up the people, elders, and scribes, seize Stephen, and drag him before the Sanhedrin.
They produce false witnesses who claim he never stops speaking against the temple and the law.
The charge: Stephen said Jesus would destroy the temple and change the customs Moses gave — twisting Jesus’s actual teachings about the temple and the fulfillment of the law.

f.w: change the customs which Moses delivered us

n: Everyone in the council stares at Stephen and sees his face shining like an angel’s — like Moses coming down from the mount. Heaven is visibly with the accused.
